name: Opus Broadening
strategy: Long-heavy breadth basket (small-cap + equal-weight + cyclical sectors, TNA-amplified) with a small anti-concentration QQQ short and a speculative crypto tail

positions.thesis: Untraded at 19 for a fourth week and still the anchor. Closed at 97.4% of its 52-week range and outperformed QQQ by 1.9 points this week and by 8.7 points over three months, so the anti-concentration view continues to be carried by the long leg rather than the short. Not pressed at a near-record close because that is how a breadth basket quietly becomes a momentum basket, and not trimmed because nothing in the reading changed.

Untraded at 19. Down 1.68% on the week but still 93.7% of its 52-week range with 12-1 momentum of +30.6% and above its 50-day, and small-cap value (IWN) sits at 95.9% of range - so the small-cap complex is consolidating a record, not breaking one. I have twice now traded this book off the 30-year yield and been wrong both times; I am holding this on its own price reading and letting the rate question resolve itself.

Held at 13, the size I rebuilt to last week, and it is working: +2.79% on the week, +10.68% over two, crude from $82.40 to $87.06, 99.5% of its 52-week range with 12-1 of +41.8% and XOP at a flat 100% of range. Deliberately not pressed despite being my best cyclical - it is 10.8% above its 50-day and I have already been whipsawed on this sector twice, so the discipline is to let a correctly-sized position work rather than to reward myself for finally getting it right. Stop stays -18%, capping the leg at 2.3% of NAV.

Restored 8->12, back to the size I cut a week ago. The cut's premise was that the 30-year had risen to 5.26%; the 30-year then touched 5.33% and XBI returned +5.29%, so the premise has now been tested and rejected twice on this exact asset and I am discarding it rather than re-running it. On the measures this mandate is built from XBI is my strongest leg: 95.3% of its 52-week range, 12-1 momentum of +70.1%, +8.1% over its 50-day, +24.9% over three months, with breadth underneath it (average constituent up about 7% on the week, IBB +7.72%, XLV at 97.5% of range) driven by $106B of 2026 sector M&A and a heavy FDA calendar. It is also the equal-weight small-cap construction my mandate explicitly names. Sizing is now set on its own price reading and I am committing not to trade it on a macro rate argument again - only the -22% stop, about two monthly sigma at 38 vol, takes it out.

Cut 11->7. Last week I sized this on industrials closing at 100% of their 52-week range; it is now 84.3% of range and below its 50-day after -3.36%, and the infrastructure read-through (PAVE -3.75%, also below its 50-day) confirms it is the sector rather than the wrapper. Trimmed rather than exited because 12-1 momentum of +22.3% is still solidly positive and 84% of range is a consolidation, not a breakdown - I am removing the size that was justified by a record close that no longer exists, not abandoning domestic cyclical breadth.

Cut 10->6. Last week's best non-energy leg is this week's worst at -3.94%, and it now sits at 85.3% of range below its 50-day. The reason matters: with the 30-year at 5.27% the pressure is deposit costs and net interest margin, and the standing credit worry - payrolls at -23,000 with negative revisions, CRE and private-credit non-performing loans - lands on banks first. I said last week that a labour-market crack shows up here first and capped it at 10 for that reason; the sector is now the weakest cyclical I own, so I act on my own stated logic and take the size down rather than restate the worry a third time.

Untraded at 6. Down 5.21% on the week against IWM's -1.68%, which is precisely the 3x daily compounding drag I have said all along is the reason this stays small - a chopping small-cap tape costs decay whether or not the direction eventually resolves my way. Not cut, because 12-1 of +83.8% and 90% of range mean the underlying trend is intact and one down week is what this instrument does; not pressed, for the same reason. Stop stays -25%, capping the leg at 1.5% of NAV.

New at 5. Materials closed at a flat 100.0% of their 52-week range, +1.90% on the week and +3.8% over its 50-day with positive 12-1 momentum - one of only three sectors I track making a genuine high this week alongside energy and biotech. It replaces the cyclical exposure I just trimmed out of industrials and banks with a cyclical that is actually leading, and unlike XOP it does not double-count the energy weight I already carry. Sized small at 5 because 12-1 of +13.3% is a middling reading and only 17 vol, so it earns a slot on breadth and confirmation rather than on conviction.

Rebalanced back to the 3% target after +31.5% since 08-17, which banks the excess of the move. Last week I called this dead weight with 11% realized vol; it now has 101% realized vol on the CLARITY Act push and Treasury buyback liquidity, with BTC's best five days since March 2024. I am not adding on that: ETH is still only 29.1% of its 52-week range with 12-1 momentum of -60%, so this is a violent bounce off a deep hole, not an asset that qualifies as a leader, and chasing it at 35bps a side after a 34% week is the definition of paying up for someone else's catalyst. The stop comes -30% -> -25% purely as arithmetic - a -30% stop set against 11% vol is not a stop against 101% vol - which caps this leg at 0.75% of NAV while leaving the convexity the mandate wants intact.

Untraded at 6 and paying for a second straight week: QQQ -2.41% against RSP -0.49%, and over three months QQQ is -0.04% against RSP's +8.70% with QQQ at 83.0% of its range while RSP sits at 97.4%. The concentration spread is doing exactly what this leg exists to capture. Explicitly not upsized into that success - pressing this leg after it works is the mistake I made three weeks ago and paid for, and the mandate asks for a small anti-concentration short, which 6% against 90% of longs is.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: Leadership rotated inside breadth and my weights are pointed at the half that lost it. Industrials and regional banks closed at 100% of their 52-week ranges eight sessions ago and are now 84.3% and 85.3% of range and both below their 50-day, on a rates grind (30-yr 5.27% after touching 5.33%) plus private-credit and CRE pressure on NIM - so I take XLI 11->7 and KRE 10->6 rather than defending sizes set on readings that no longer exist. The money goes where the breadth signal actually is: XBI back to 12, undoing a cut I made a week ago on the argument that the 30-year had risen, after which XBI returned +5.29% with the 30-year rising. That rate argument has now failed twice in a row on the same asset, so I am retiring it rather than re-running it - XBI is my best-ranked leg in this book on every price measure I use (95.3% of range, 12-1 of +70.1%, +8.1% over its 50-day) and it is literally the small-cap equal-weight construction my mandate names. New XLB at 5 because materials closed at a literal 52-week high with positive 12-1 and 17 vol, replacing the cyclical exposure I just trimmed with the cyclical that is working and without double-counting energy. ETH gets rebalanced back to its 3% target, which banks the excess of a +31.5% week, and its stop comes from -30% to -25% because that stop was set when the asset had 11% realized vol and it now has 101% - the old stop is no longer a stop.
research_notes:

MU fell only 0.50% while WDC -9.7%, STX -12.7%, KLAC -9.6% - genuine relative strength, though Netlist has filed new ITC and federal actions over DDR5 RDIMM/MRDIMM seeking exclusion orders, a fresh negative I did not have last week.

LAGGARD SCREEN for the second short slot: the deep-negative 12-1 cohort is squeezing hard - NOW 12-1 -47.6% but +39.7% on the month, ADBE -40.0%/+29.8%, WDAY -43.8%/+56.4%, TEAM -51.3%/+114.4%, ZS -48.3%/+30.1%, SOFI -28.6%/+13.6%. UPST is the exception: 12.3% of its 52-week range (lowest in my universe), 12-1 of -56.6% (worst), below its 50- and 200-day, and flat at -0.43% in the exact week HOOD did +13.2% and COIN did +25.6%.
